metaDescription: Turn Markdown into a real .docx: headings, bold, italic, code, links, nested lists, quotes, code blocks and tables. Opens in Word, LibreOffice and Google Docs.
intro: Convert Markdown notes or documentation into a Word file without Pandoc.
why:
The converter builds the Office Open XML package itself: styles for Heading 1 to 6, quote and code paragraphs, a numbering definition for bullets and numbered lists with nesting, hyperlinks, tables with borders and a bold header row, and document properties. The result was opened with python-docx and converted to PDF with LibreOffice during testing.

Images, footnotes, task-list checkboxes and fancy typography are not converted, and styling is basic. For publishing-quality output use Pandoc with a reference document.

The file is read in your browser and is not uploaded anywhere.
howTo: Open it and adjust fonts or styles as needed.

faq.a: Headings, paragraphs, bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, links, nested lists, quotes, fenced code, tables and rules.

faq.q: Does Word complain when opening it?
faq.a: The package follows the standard structure and opened in LibreOffice and python-docx; if Word reports a problem, tell us which Markdown triggered it.
The file is read in your browser and is not uploaded anywhere.
